request.text: What is the voltage on voltmeter?

solution.item: *** Solution by TINA assisted by AI ***
The voltage for graph number 0 has been set to 0V.
The voltage for graph number 3 has been set to 5V.
At first we calculate the total resistance between the generator nodes (VS1)
V and R1 connected in series so Rb=V+R1=1Ohm+1Ohm=2Ohm
R3 and Rb connected in series so Ra=R3+Rb=1Ohm+2Ohm=3Ohm
The total resistance is Ra = 3Ohm
Now we calculate the voltage on VM1
We know that the voltage between VS1 nodes is 5V.
The voltage for graph number 2 has been set to 1.67V.
The components R3,Rb connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 5V
R3 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on R3 is R3/Ra*5V = 1.67V
The components R3,Rb connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 5V
Rb is in the voltage divider so the voltage on Rb is Rb/Ra*5V = 3.33V
The voltage for graph number 1 has been set to 3.33V.
The components V,R1 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 3.33V
V is in the voltage divider so the voltage on V is V/Rb*3.33V = 1.67V
The components V,R1 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 3.33V
R1 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on R1 is R1/Rb*3.33V = 1.67V
To answer the original question: because the voltmeter connected to nodes 1,0 so the voltage on voltmeter is 3.33V
